hook: Two bicycle makers from Ohio who made the first powered airplane flight.

pages.x: In 1878 their father brought home a toy helicopter made of bamboo, paper and cork, driven by a rubber band. Wilbur and Orville Wright played with it until it broke, then built their own.
The brothers never finished high school, and never married. In Dayton, Ohio, they ran a printing press, then from 1892 a bicycle shop, which paid for their experiments with flying machines.
Watching birds, Wilbur saw that they twist the tips of their wings to keep their balance. Twisting an empty cardboard box in his hands, he saw how to twist a wing in the same way.
pages.fx: Control in three directions, rolling, climbing and turning, is still how every airplane is steered.

pages.x: For their gliders they needed strong, steady winds, soft sand to land on and no crowds. They found them at Kitty Hawk, on the coast of North Carolina, and camped there every autumn.
The published tables on how wings lift turned out to be wrong. So in 1901 they built a wind tunnel, a wooden box with a fan, and tested some 200 shapes of wing.
pages.fx: With the results they designed wings and propellers that worked, founding the science of aeronautics.

pages.x: On 17 December 1903 Orville flew their Flyer for 12 seconds and 37 metres: the first controlled, powered airplane flight. Wilbur had won a coin toss to go first three days before, but stalled. That day he flew 260 metres.
Few people believed them at first. In 1908 Wilbur flew in France, swooping and circling under perfect control, and stunned the crowds. "We are beaten," said a French pilot.
Wilbur died of typhoid in 1912. Orville lived until 1948, long enough to see planes fly faster than sound.
The Wright brothers invented the airplane. Just 66 years after their first flight, people walked on the Moon, and a scrap of their Flyer went with them.
pts: Made the first powered, controlled airplane flight
Invented the way airplanes are steered
